description:
The Carl-August-Heckscher-Schule in Munich is a state-run special education center and a school for the sick, closely affiliated with the kbo-Heckscher-Klinikum for child and adolescent psychiatry. Its main campus is located at Deisenhofener Straße 28 in Munich-Giesing, complemented by several external branches in Upper Bavaria, including Rosenheim, Rottmannshöhe, Landsberg am Lech, and Haar. The school caters to children and adolescents of all school types who require partial inpatient or inpatient stays in clinics due to psychological illnesses or disorders.

The pedagogical concept of the Carl-August-Heckscher-Schule is highly individualized and tailored to the specific needs of the student patients. Instruction follows the curricula of the respective school types but is flexibly adapted to the health situation and individual learning requirements. A distinctive feature is the close collaboration of the 65 teachers with the treating doctors and therapists on-site to ensure holistic support. With 271 students in the 2024/25 school year, the school provides intensive care in small learning groups.

Special offerings include a focus on emotional and social development. The school also serves as a consultation school for children and adolescents with autistic behaviors and provides a Mobile Special Education Service (MSD). This MSD includes counseling services for teachers, parents, and students, even after their clinic stay, as well as training courses on 'Pedagogy in case of illness'. Care hours are from 7:30 AM to 4:00 PM on legal school days. The District of Upper Bavaria is responsible for the material costs (Sachaufwandsträger), while the school itself is a state institution under the Government of Upper Bavaria. The head of the school is Bernhard Ruppert.
summary_en: The Carl-August-Heckscher-Schule in Munich is a state-run special education center and school for the sick, specializing in supporting children and adolescents with emotional, social, and psychological challenges during their clinic stays. It offers individualized instruction, close collaboration with therapists, and a Mobile Special Education Service, including for autistic behaviors.
summary_de: Die Carl-August-Heckscher-Schule in München ist ein staatliches Förderzentrum und eine Schule für Kranke, spezialisiert auf die Förderung von Kindern und Jugendlichen mit emotionalen, sozialen und psychischen Herausforderungen während ihres Klinikaufenthalts. The Anni-Braun-Schule in Munich, a special education center with a focus on language development, is a specialized educational institution located at Musenbergstraße 32, 81929 Munich. It is part of the Special Education Center for Hearing and Language in the Johanneskirchen district (also known as Bogenhausen) and is dedicated to the comprehensive support of approximately 253 students from all over Upper Bavaria who exhibit speech or language problems, such as speech impediments, comprehension difficulties, or articulation issues. With a dedicated staff of 46 teachers, the school offers an educational concept based on the Mittelschule curriculum, aiming to enable students to achieve the qualified Mittelschulabschluss or, for high-achieving students, the intermediate school certificate via the M-Zug.

Among the special offerings of the Anni-Braun-Schule are a Therapeutic Day Care Center and a Therapeutic Residence, which ensure holistic care and support. For grades 5 to 7, full-day classes and open full-day groups are offered in the afternoon, allowing for flexible and intensive supervision. Furthermore, there are cooperation classes and counseling services that support the academic and personal growth of the students. The school also functions as a teacher training school (Seminarschule), highlighting its role in teacher education. Founded in 1955, the Anni-Braun-Schule is supported by the District of Upper Bavaria as its financial sponsor. Its location within a specialized school center provides a conducive environment for students with special linguistic needs.

description:
The Staatliche Dieter-Hildebrandt-Wirtschaftsschule München, founded in 2003, is a renowned vocational preparatory school in Munich that combines comprehensive general education with solid basic vocational training in the field of business and administration. The school is named after the famous Munich cabaret artist Dieter Hildebrandt, a unique naming convention in Germany. With 351 students and 27 teachers (as of 2024/25), it offers an engaging learning environment. It leads its students to an intermediate school leaving certificate (Mittlerer Schulabschluss), which allows graduates to shorten a commercial apprenticeship by up to one year.

The school operates at two locations: a main office in Munich-Sendling (Meindlstr. 8 a / Plinganserstraße 28, 81369 Munich) and an external branch in Oberhaching. It offers both a two-stage commercial school (grades 10-11) and a three-stage commercial school (grades 8-10), both fully developed. The pedagogical concept aims to attract highly motivated young people with a particular interest in practical business or administration issues. The curriculum is interdisciplinary and competence-oriented, designed to establish a direct link to professional life. General subjects include German, English, Mathematics, Social Studies, Religion/Ethics, and Sports, complemented by vocational subjects such as Business Management and Control, Information Processing, and the Practice Firm (Übungsunternehmen), where students can experience the reality of a commercial profession.

Notably, from 2018 to 2023, the school participated as a pilot school in the “Leistung macht Schule – LemaS” initiative to promote high-achieving students and now acts as a multiplier in the second funding phase. Specific care services beyond regular instruction are not explicitly listed, but the focus is on intensive vocational preparation. The school is state-owned.

description:
The Staatliche Berufsoberschule für Technik München, located at Orleansstraße 44 in the heart of Munich, is a public, state-run educational institution dedicated to vocational further education and the acquisition of higher school leaving certificates. As part of the Bavarian Vocational Upper Secondary School system, it enables graduates with an intermediate school leaving certificate and completed vocational training to achieve the Fachhochschulreife (university of applied sciences entrance qualification), subject-specific university entrance qualification, or the general university entrance qualification by acquiring a second foreign language. The school offers the technical specialization in grades 12 and 13 and also has a preparatory class (Vorklasse) that specifically prepares students who have obtained their intermediate educational qualification through vocational school or vocational college for the demands of the 12th grade. [cite: 2, 2 (Berufsoberschule (Bayern) - Wikipedia)]

A prominent feature of the school is its "Inclusion School Profile" (Schulprofil Inklusion). This means that the Staatliche Berufsoberschule für Technik München pursues a comprehensive educational concept that implements individual support for all students in teaching and school life, regardless of their special needs. General education teachers collaborate with special education professionals, where appropriate, to facilitate inclusive learning and accommodate the diversity of the student body. [cite: 2, 2 (Schulen mit Profil Inklusion - schule-oberfranken.de), 6 (BayEUG: Art. 30b Inklusive Schule)]

With 92 students and 2 teachers in the 2024/25 school year, the school offers a personal learning atmosphere. Instruction focuses on core subjects such as German, Mathematics, and English, supplemented by the option to choose French, Latin, or Spanish as a second foreign language to achieve the general university entrance qualification. [cite: 2, 2 (Berufsoberschule (Bayern) - Wikipedia)]

The school is centrally located in Munich, ensuring good accessibility by public transport and providing students with access to the city's diverse cultural and professional opportunities. As a "Seminarschule," it also contributes to the training of future teachers. The school is led by Principal OStDin Simone Schwensfeier.
summary_en: The Staatliche Berufsoberschule für Technik München is a state-run vocational upper secondary school in Munich specializing in technology. It enables graduates with an intermediate school leaving certificate and vocational training to acquire higher educational qualifications up to the general university entrance qualification. The school is distinguished by its "Inclusion School Profile," offering individualized support for all students. [cite: 2, 2 (Berufsoberschule (Bayern) - Wikipedia)]
summary_de: Die Staatliche Berufsoberschule für Technik München ist eine staatliche Berufsoberschule in München mit dem Schwerpunkt Technik. Sie ermöglicht Absolventen mit mittlerem Schulabschluss und Berufsausbildung den Erwerb höherer Bildungsabschlüsse bis zur allgemeinen Hochschulreife und zeichnet sich durch ihr "Schulprofil Inklusion" aus, das individuelle Förderung für alle Schülerinnen und Schüler bietet. [cite: 2, 2 (Berufsoberschule (Bayern) - Wikipedia)]

description:
The Musenbergschule in Munich is a specialized special education center with a focus on hearing impairment, dedicated to the comprehensive education and support of hard-of-hearing, deaf, and hearing-impaired children and adolescents. Located in the Munich district of Johanneskirchen, the school is part of a larger school complex and is supported by the District of Upper Bavaria as the school maintenance organization. With 214 students and 60 teachers (as of the 2024/25 school year), the Musenbergschule offers primary and middle school levels, which follow the curricula of general schools but include specific adaptations in German language for students with hearing impairments.

The school's pedagogical concept is designed to promote hearing ability through targeted auditory education and the use of state-of-the-art technology, such as classroom hearing systems in combination with individual hearing aids. Classrooms are acoustically and technically optimized and equipped with laptops, projectors, and interactive whiteboards. In addition to qualified hearing and deaf teachers who teach in small classes, the development of sign language skills and lip-reading is also supported to meet the diverse communicative needs of the students. The school cooperates closely with hearing aid acousticians and ENT doctors.

Special offerings include a School Preparatory Facility (SVE) for children aged three to six, a Pedagogical-Audiological Counseling Center, mobile services for children in mainstream schools and daycares, as well as a Therapeutic Day Care Center and a Therapeutic Residential Home. The school also offers general school leaving certificates and guides students through internships and projects towards vocational readiness, supporting career choices in cooperation with the employment agency. As a training school for teachers, it also contributes to teacher education. The Musenbergschule provides full-day schooling in an open format and in other facilities.
summary_en: The Musenbergschule in Munich is a special education center for hearing-impaired children and adolescents, with 214 students and 60 teachers. It provides primary and middle school education with a special focus on auditory education, language development, and the use of modern technology. The offerings are complemented by a School Preparatory Facility, counseling services, and care options such as a school boarding house and a Therapeutic Day Care Center.
summary_de: Die Musenbergschule in München ist ein Förderzentrum für hörgeschädigte Kinder und Jugendliche mit 214 Schülern und 60 Lehrkräften. description:
Mittelschule München, Franz-Nißl-Straße 55, is an established educational institution located in the Allach district of Munich, founded in 1936. Led by Principal Dominika Neresheimer, the school currently provides comprehensive education to 365 students, supported by a dedicated team of 31 teachers. The school's pedagogical concept is designed to offer diverse educational pathways, including preparation for the Einfacher Mittelschulabschluss (EMA) and the Mittlere Reife through specialized M-classes (M7, M9, M10). A particular focus is placed on language development with the DeutschPLUS (GMS) program and English as a foreign language. 

The school is distinguished by a wide range of special programs and projects. As a 'School against Racism - School with Courage,' it actively promotes tolerance and civic courage. The school's own radio station provides students with a platform for creative expression and media literacy. Comprehensive childcare services are offered as part of the full-day schooling program (Gebundener Ganztag, GGTS). Career orientation plays a central role, supported by close cooperation with the Federal Employment Agency, which includes individual career counseling and company visits, such as to Deutsche Bahn. The profile is further enriched by projects like K.I.D.S. (e.g., puppet making, unicycling), boxing workshops for girls, and participation in Girl's Day and Boys' Day. The school also maintains numerous partnerships with local organizations such as Kolping München, the Lions Club Münchner Kindl, and the Johanniter, which enhance school life. The school building, constructed between 1936 and 1940 by Sep Ruf, is an architecturally notable part of the Allach district.
summary_en: Mittelschule München, Franz-Nißl-Straße 55, founded in 1936, provides diverse educational pathways up to Mittlere Reife for 365 students under Principal Dominika Neresheimer. description:
Mittelschule München, Sambergerstraße 14, is an established educational institution located in the Parkstadt Solln district of Munich. The school was founded in the 1967/68 school year as a comprehensive school (Gemeinschaftsschule) and was divided into a primary and secondary school (Hauptschule, now Mittelschule) in 1975. It is named after the renowned portrait painter Leo Samberger. In the 2024/25 school year, 114 students attend the school, taught by 9 teachers.

As a fully developed Mittelschule, it offers grades 5 to 10 and enables students to acquire the qualified Mittelschule certificate (qualifizierender Mittelschulabschluss) as well as preparation for the intermediate secondary school certificate (mittlerer Schulabschluss, M-Zug). The pedagogical concept of Bavarian Mittelschulen, which is also practiced at Sambergerstraße, places great emphasis on personality development, individual support, and a consistent career and practical orientation. The lessons are designed to be relevant to real life and promote social and personal skills in addition to subject knowledge. The school is part of the Mittelschulverbund Süd, together with Mittelschule in der Zielstattstraße and Mittelschule München, Walliser Straße, creating a cooperative educational landscape in southern Munich.

Among the special offerings of Mittelschule Sambergerstraße is the DeutschPLUS (GMS) program, which specifically supports students with non-German mother tongues. In terms of childcare, the school offers open all-day care (Ganztagsbetreuung) as well as midday care (Mittagsbetreuung), which can also be utilized on a daily basis. A remarkable social commitment is demonstrated by the breakfast initiative, where students receive healthy breakfast options twice a week, prepared by a dedicated mother and students. Furthermore, the school participates in the EU School Program – Fruit, through which children receive free regional and seasonal fruit to develop healthy eating habits.

The school is located at Sambergerstraße 14 in 81477 Munich, in the Parkstadt Solln district. The school district extends from Kistlerhofstraße in the north to Wilhelm-Leibl-Straße in the south, and from Ludwigshöher-Straße in the west to Stäblistraße in the east. The school's facilities are tailored to the needs of a modern Mittelschule to ensure a supportive learning environment. The official website of the school is www.mssamberger.edupage.org.
summary_en: Mittelschule München, Sambergerstraße 14, is an established educational institution in Munich's Parkstadt Solln, serving 114 students with 9 teachers. It offers grades 5-10, emphasizing personality development, individual support, and career orientation. Special programs include DeutschPLUS, open all-day and midday care, a breakfast initiative, and the EU School Program – Fruit.

description:
Karlsgymnasium München-Pasing is a traditional grammar school with a humanistic and linguistic focus, situated by the Pasinger Stadtpark in Munich. The school was founded in 1910 as a royal humanistic 'Progymnasium' and is housed in a listed Art Nouveau building dating from 1909/10. Currently, approximately 691 students attend the institution, taught by 60 teachers. Since the 2017/18 school year, the nine-year Gymnasium (G9) curriculum has been offered again.

The pedagogical concept of Karlsgymnasium places a strong emphasis on comprehensive linguistic education. Latin is taught as the first foreign language from the 5th grade, followed by English from the 6th grade. From the 8th grade, students can choose between Greek and French. For late-starting foreign languages, Italian is available from the 11th grade. The Gymnasium enables students to acquire the 'Latinum' certificate and offers numerous elective courses in various fields. A special feature is its musical focus, including a string class, as well as projects promoting student responsibility, which encourage active participation in school life.

As a 'Seminarschule' (training school), Karlsgymnasium contributes to the education of future teachers. The school offers an open all-day school program to support and encourage students beyond regular lessons. Its location by the Pasinger Stadtpark provides a green and tranquil learning environment. Karlsgymnasium has received multiple awards for its achievements in the past, including top rankings in Abitur results and successes in competitions. The school is operated by the Free State of Bavaria.
summary_en: Karlsgymnasium München-Pasing is a humanistic and linguistic grammar school with 691 students and 60 teachers, founded in 1910. The school is a training school, has a musical focus, promotes student responsibility through projects, and offers an open all-day program.

description:
Maximiliansgymnasium München, often referred to as "Max," is a renowned co-educational humanist and European Gymnasium under state sponsorship, centrally located in Schwabing, not far from Münchner Freiheit. Founded in 1849 by King Maximilian II, it is the city's third-oldest Gymnasium and is housed in a listed Art Nouveau building that offers modern learning and living spaces. Currently, approximately 720 students attend the school, taught by about 55 full-time teachers.

The pedagogical concept of Maximiliansgymnasium is characterized by a strong emphasis on classical languages and natural sciences. The language sequence begins in the 5th grade with Latin, followed by English in the 6th grade, and Ancient Greek in the 8th grade. Optionally, Spanish can be chosen from the 10th or 11th grade, with the possibility of dropping Latin. This approach promotes a comprehensive education that considers both the humanities and the exact sciences. The Gymnasium is proud of its tradition and its famous alumni, such as Max Planck and Werner Heisenberg.

Special offerings include an Open All-Day School (oGTS), which has been provided free of charge for lower-grade children since 2016/17. It includes lunch, an "active break," and supervised study time for homework and learning material on four school days (Mon-Thu), supported by qualified staff. Furthermore, the school offers comprehensive counseling and support services, including school counseling, school psychology, compensation for disadvantages, and tutoring programs. A well-equipped library, elective courses, and school trips complement school life. The school values a socially active community. In addition to the historic building, the facilities include modern amenities and sports facilities. Its central location in Schwabing provides an attractive environment with good connectivity.
summary_en: Maximiliansgymnasium Munich is a state-sponsored humanist and European Gymnasium in Schwabing, founded in 1849. It offers a comprehensive education with a focus on classical languages and natural sciences, alongside an Open All-Day School. Known for famous alumni like Max Planck, the school combines tradition in a listed Art Nouveau building with modern learning spaces and diverse support programs.
summary_de: Das Maximiliansgymnasium München ist ein staatliches humanistisches und Europäisches Gymnasium in Schwabing, gegründet 1849. description:
Wilhelmsgymnasium Munich, founded in 1559, is the oldest grammar school in Upper Bavaria and a state-run humanistic gymnasium with a long tradition. It is centrally located in Munich's Lehel district, at Thierschstraße 46, at the corner of Maximilianstraße, directly by the Maxmonument. The immediate proximity to important institutions such as the Government of Upper Bavaria and the Bavarian State Parliament (Maximilianeum), as well as to the English Garden with the Eisbach wave, shapes the school's cultural and urban environment. 

In the 2024/25 school year, 536 students attend the gymnasium, taught by 50 teachers. The pedagogical concept of Wilhelmsgymnasium sees itself as a “lighthouse of humanistic education” and places a strong focus on the classical languages Latin and Greek, which are taught from the 5th and 8th grades respectively. This linguistic education aims to promote thoroughness, systematic work, perseverance, and methodological accuracy. The language offerings are complemented by English from the 6th grade, as well as late-starting foreign languages such as Italian and Polish from the 11th grade. Chinese is also offered as an elective course. 

As a cultural gymnasium, Wilhelmsgymnasium places great importance on aesthetic education and the development of a mature personality through engagement in music, art, literature, and theater, for example, in choir, orchestra, or theater groups. Special offers include partnerships with the Weimar Classic Foundation and LMU (Archaeology), which provide students with in-depth insights into cultural and scientific fields. The gymnasium offers an open all-day program for grades 5 to 7, including lunch, and fosters a familial school climate under the motto “WG = Wir Gemeinsam” (We Together), based on politeness, respect, and tolerance. The school is led by Michael Hotz.

description:

As an open all-day school ("offene Ganztagsschule"), the Wittelsbacher-Gymnasium provides supervised study time and a variety of leisure activities from Monday to Thursday until 4:10 PM.

description:
The Marieluise-Fleißer-Realschule (MFR) is a state-run Realschule in Munich, established in the 2003/2004 school year and named after the writer Marieluise Fleißer in 2005. Since September 2021, the school has been located in a modern new building at Aschauer Straße 9, 81549 Munich, having previously been situated at Schwanthalerstraße 87. The new site features a six-stream Realschule with a triple sports hall, underground parking, and a children's house, providing excellent infrastructure for daily school life. The school is attended by approximately 907 students and taught by 60 teachers, led by headmistress Birgitt Michelly-Jipp. 

The MFR's educational concept is characterized by a comprehensive profile that actively promotes inclusion and takes a stand against discrimination as a 'School without Racism – School with Courage'. Special offerings include the SPRINT program, a bilingual program, and participation in the Erasmus+ program, which facilitates international experiences. French is offered as a foreign language within the elective subject groups. As an open all-day school, the MFR also provides childcare services that meet the needs of families. Its location in the Obergiesing-Fasangarten district offers good connectivity and a diverse environment for students.
summary_en: The Marieluise-Fleißer-Realschule in Munich is a state Realschule with 907 students and 60 teachers, housed in a modern new building at Aschauer Straße 9 since 2021. It features an inclusive profile, commitment as a 'School without Racism – School with Courage,' and special programs like SPRINT, bilingual offerings, and Erasmus+. French is offered as a foreign language, and the school operates as an open all-day school.

description:
Founded in 1864, the Oskar-von-Miller-Gymnasium Munich is a distinguished Gymnasium situated in the vibrant Schwabing district of Munich, conveniently located near Münchner Freiheit. With an enrollment of 1054 students and a faculty of 78 teachers (as of the 2024/25 academic year), it stands as a prominent educational institution within the city. The school is housed in a historic building at Siegfriedstraße 22, 80803 Munich, which is recognized as an architectural monument. This building underwent extensive general renovation from 2018 to 2023 and was officially reopened in October 2024.

The pedagogical philosophy of the Oskar-von-Miller-Gymnasium is characterized by a strong emphasis on modern languages, while also offering Latin as the primary foreign language. The language curriculum includes Latin, English, French, and Italian, with distinct language sequences such as Latin, English, French, and Latin, English, Italian. A significant feature is the bilingual program in French, which culminates in the AbiBac, a prestigious dual German and French Abitur, equipping students with exceptional international qualifications. As a "Seminarschule," the gymnasium plays a crucial role in teacher training, underscoring its dedication to high educational standards and pedagogical innovation. The school operates under the G8 system, providing an accelerated pathway to the Abitur.

Beyond its core academic offerings, the school provides a diverse array of special programs and extracurricular activities. These encompass subjects like Mathematics, German, DaZ (German as a second language), Physics, Chemistry, and Computer Science. The school integrates modern learning tools, such as the Mathegym platform, to support students across various subjects. Cultural and creative development is fostered through initiatives like "Oskar sings," the U02-Theater, and OskarTV, which offer students platforms to cultivate their talents. Project seminars, such as the history seminar exploring the school's architectural heritage, provide in-depth learning experiences.

The school's location in Schwabing provides a stimulating urban environment with excellent public transportation links and access to cultural institutions. While specific daily care services (e.g., after-school care) are not explicitly detailed, the comprehensive educational and extracurricular programs contribute to a supportive and enriching learning atmosphere. The school's commitment to preserving its historical legacy, combined with contemporary pedagogical approaches and international programs, establishes it as a distinguished Gymnasium in Munich.
summary_en: Founded in 1864, the Oskar-von-Miller-Gymnasium Munich is a renowned Gymnasium in Schwabing. It features a modern language profile with Latin as the first foreign language, a bilingual French program leading to the AbiBac, and serves as a teacher training school. Housed in a recently renovated, historically protected building, the gymnasium emphasizes comprehensive education and diverse extracurricular activities.

description:
Asam-Gymnasium München, a state-run educational institution located in the Obergiesing district in the south of Munich's city center, was founded in 1935 and has been situated at its current address, Schlierseestraße 20, since 1964. With 1192 students and 93 teachers, it offers a comprehensive educational program. The school is known for its MINT focus (HoriZONTec) and features both a scientific-technological and a linguistic branch, the latter introduced in 2005. The language sequence includes English, Latin, French, and Italian, with French also offered as a late-starting foreign language from the 11th grade.

As a seminar school, Asam-Gymnasium trains prospective teachers in subjects such as Mathematics, Physics, Biology, Chemistry, German, English, History, Sports, and Protestant Religious Education, underscoring its high pedagogical quality. The pedagogical concept is characterized by openness, plurality, and high educational and upbringing standards, fostering a friendly and learning-conducive environment. The school was the first public gymnasium in Munich to establish a compulsory full-day program for grades 5 to 8, complemented by lunch provisions.

The school's facilities are described as very modern. In addition to regular classes, Asam-Gymnasium offers a wide range of special features and elective courses, including the Asamesischer Zirkus, student exchange programs with France, a school first-aid service, performing arts, a library team, tutoring programs, and numerous musical offerings such as wind instrument classes, choirs, a jazz band, and a wind orchestra. Projects like "Jugend forscht" and various working groups (AK Green, AK Rainbow, AK Schulküche, AK Feste, Streitschlichter) also promote the holistic development of students. Asam-Gymnasium also prepares students with a Mittlerer Schulabschluss for the Gymnasium's upper secondary level. It provides a demanding, holistic, and high-quality school experience for engaged learners.
summary_en: Asam-Gymnasium München is a state gymnasium in Obergiesing with a MINT focus and a linguistic branch. It offers a compulsory full-day program, serves as a seminar school, and promotes students through diverse musical, athletic, and social activities. The school is characterized by a modern environment and high educational standards.

description:
Gisela-Gymnasium München, founded in 1904, is a renowned Gymnasium located in the heart of Schwabing, directly adjacent to Elisabethplatz. Under the leadership of Headmaster Herr OStD Christoph Pfaffendorf, the listed Art Nouveau building contributes to the distinctive charm of this Munich district. The school sees itself as a cosmopolitan "European School" and "School without Racism – School with Courage," firmly rooted in Munich while maintaining international contacts. A special focus is placed on the inclusion of hearing-impaired students, who are supported through dedicated "A-classes" with technical room equipment, targeted assistance, and a cooperative climate of mutual respect. School dogs and reading dogs also enrich the pedagogical work.

The pedagogical concept is based on the "Good Spirit of Gisela-Gymnasium," which prioritizes human interaction, communication, and the imparting of intercultural competencies to prepare students for life in a united Europe. The Gymnasium offers the Abitur after nine school years (G9) and features a natural science-technological branch and a linguistic branch starting from the 8th grade. In addition to core subjects, a variety of languages such as English, Latin, French, Spanish, Japanese, and Russian are offered. As a MINT-friendly school (STEM-friendly) and a basketball support school, whose team has already won the Bavarian championship, Gisela-Gymnasium fosters both scientific talents and athletic excellence. The offerings are complemented by diverse elective subjects like art, music, theater, and chess.

For after-school care, the school provides an open all-day program (OGTS), implemented in cooperation with Condrobs e.V. This program, which begins at 1:00 PM, includes qualified homework supervision for 5th and 6th graders from 2:00 PM to 4:30 PM, as well as meaningful leisure activities. The school day starts at 8:00 AM and ends no later than 5:25 PM. With approximately 1017 students and 77 teachers, Gisela-Gymnasium creates a liberal atmosphere of mutual respect and tolerance that recognizes and promotes the diversity of lifestyles.
summary_en: Gisela-Gymnasium Munich is a traditional "European School" in the heart of Schwabing, characterized by an inclusive concept for hearing-impaired students and a cosmopolitan pedagogical mission. It offers natural science-technological and linguistic branches (G9) with a wide range of languages (including Japanese, Russian), MINT promotion, and is a basketball support school. An open all-day program with homework supervision completes its profile.

description:
Luitpold-Gymnasium München, founded in 1891 as the Royal Luitpold District Realschule, is a traditional educational institution in the heart of Munich. Originally designed with a strong focus on natural sciences and modern foreign languages to directly prepare students for the demands of the modern professional world, the school has continuously evolved. Since 1983, it has been co-educational, now providing a dynamic learning environment for 918 students and 73 teachers.

The pedagogical concept of Luitpold-Gymnasium is characterized by a combination of sound knowledge transfer and the promotion of intellectual abilities. A central concern is to educate students towards openness to the world, tolerance, and personal responsibility, which is supported by current topics in lessons as well as social and charitable projects.

Special offers and focal points of the school include the MINT sector, with initiatives like robotics, as well as music (e.g., Big Band) and sports (e.g., events). International engagement is highlighted by the Erasmus+ program. An environmental club (Umwelt-AG) and cooperation with the Residenztheater further enrich school life.

Currently, Luitpold-Gymnasium is located at Seeaustraße 1 in the Lehel district, near the English Garden. For the 2025/2026 school year, a move to Elektrastraße 61 is planned to allow for a new building at the current site, which is expected to be ready by the 2030/31 school year. The school also offers an open all-day school (OGTS) with homework supervision.

description:
Klenze-Gymnasium München, a state-run public school under the patronage of the Free State of Bavaria, is a renowned natural science and technology-focused Gymnasium (NTG) located in Munich's Sendling district. Founded in 1921, it has evolved into an educational institution with 983 students and 73 teachers (as of the 2024/25 school year), led by headmistress Friederike Rappel. The pedagogical concept of Klenze-Gymnasium aims not only to impart a broad general academic knowledge but also to foster consistent values education. The school sees itself as a place of learning in an ever-changing world, offering an environment where the joy of learning and the development of competencies are paramount. A constructive coexistence, based on mutual respect and appreciation, as well as tolerant, open, and honest communication, are central pillars of school life.

Special offerings include a strong MINT (Mathematics, Informatics, Natural Sciences, Technology) focus and diverse musical opportunities such as wind and string instrument classes, orchestra, and wind ensemble. The language sequence includes English as the first foreign language, followed by Latin or French. Additionally, Chinese and Turkish can be chosen as late-beginning foreign languages from the 11th grade. For individual support, the Gymnasium offers remedial courses in German, French, Latin, Mathematics, Physics, and Chemistry for grades 8 to 10. The 'Future-Lounge' supports 11th graders with career and study orientation. The school's facilities were recently expanded with a new pavilion and a triple sports hall, constructed from late 2021 to January 2026. A canteen is also available.

Klenze-Gymnasium provides an open all-day program with meal services and homework supervision for grades 5 to 7. Homework supervision takes place in small groups and is overseen by qualified older students. The school is located at Wackersberger Straße 59 in 81371 Munich and is well-integrated into the Sendling district.
summary_en: Klenze-Gymnasium München is a natural science and technology-focused Gymnasium in Sendling with 983 students and 73 teachers. It offers a MINT focus, music classes, diverse languages (English, Latin, French, Chinese, Turkish), and an open all-day program with homework supervision. The pedagogical concept promotes academic knowledge, values education, and constructive cooperation in a modern learning environment.

The school is renowned for its students' successful participation in national and international competitions like the Mathematics and Physics Olympiads, and "Jugend forscht".

A distinctive feature is the support classes for gifted students, established in 1998. In cooperation with the Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München (LMU), these students receive special "Enrichment" lessons, allowing them to conduct their own experiments in the biology and physics faculties. The language offerings include English, Latin, French, Spanish, and Italian, with English and French also available as language sequences in the scientific-technological branch.

As a "Seminarschule" (training school), the MTG contributes to the education of teaching interns in various subjects. Instruction follows the G9 model, leading to the Abitur after nine school years. The school day begins at 8:00 AM and concludes no later than 4:15 PM. In addition to regular classes, numerous elective and "Plus" courses enrich the curriculum.

The historic school building, a Neo-Baroque group structure from 1898/99, was restored and expanded after war damage, including the addition of two gymnasiums. The school also offers an open full-day school operation, enhancing its childcare services. Collaborations with the German Aerospace Center (DLR) and the Technical University of Munich (TUM) underscore the school's practical orientation.
summary_en: The Maria-Theresia-Gymnasium Munich is a traditional state gymnasium with a scientific-technological and linguistic focus. It offers support classes for gifted students, is a MINT-EC school and a training school, providing a comprehensive educational program and full-day care.

description:
Pestalozzi-Gymnasium München, founded in 1965, is a state-run Gymnasium with a musical focus and an open all-day school, located at Eduard-Schmid-Str. 1, 81541 Munich. Under the leadership of Martin Mai, 847 students are currently taught by 86 teachers. The school is sponsored by the City of Munich. The pedagogical concept is based on the principles of Johann Heinrich Pestalozzi, aiming to lay a solid foundation of elementary education and holistically develop students' natural abilities to empower them for self-help. 

A special emphasis is placed on musical education, reflected in a rich offering of choirs, orchestras, and theater performances. The school is renowned for its successes in the 'Jugend musiziert' competition and places great importance on art and elective music courses. In addition to its musical profile, the Gymnasium also provides a solid education in MINT subjects (Mathematics, Informatics, Natural Sciences, Technology). The language offerings include English, French, Italian, Latin, and Spanish. 

Pestalozzi-Gymnasium is a 'School without Racism – School with Courage' and actively campaigns against discrimination. Classes run from 8:00 AM until no later than 1:55 PM, followed by a lunch break. As an open all-day school, it offers afternoon care with homework support and a variety of extracurricular activities (AGs) in areas such as handball, yoga, and climbing. School life is further enriched by numerous activities like a student newspaper, environmental projects, 'active breaks,' 'Youth Debates,' reading competitions, class trips, student exchange programs, and excursions. The school also provides counseling, mediation, and tutoring programs to support students.
summary_en: Pestalozzi-Gymnasium Munich, founded in 1965, is a musical Gymnasium with an open all-day program, fostering 847 students based on Pestalozzi's pedagogy. It is characterized by a strong focus on music and art, MINT offerings, and its commitment as a 'School without Racism – School with Courage.' The school also provides diverse care and leisure activities, along with a wide range of language options.
summary_de: Das Pestalozzi-Gymnasium München ist ein 1965 gegründetes musisches Gymnasium mit offener Ganztagsschule, das 847 Schülerinnen und Schüler nach der Pädagogik Pestalozzis fördert. description:
Michaeli-Gymnasium Munich, a state-run educational institution, was founded in 1971 and is strategically located in the vibrant Munich district of Berg am Laim. It is known for its dual orientation as a linguistic and scientific-technological Gymnasium, offering students a wide range of academic opportunities. With a community of 1268 students and 92 dedicated teachers, the school ensures individual support and a rich educational program.

In the linguistic branch, comprehensive instruction is offered in English, French, Latin, and Spanish, with Spanish standing out as one of the curriculum's special features. The scientific-technological branch places a strong emphasis on MINT subjects (Mathematics, Informatics, Natural Sciences, Technology) to specifically foster young talents in these future-oriented disciplines and prepare them for academic and professional challenges.

The pedagogical mission of Michaeli-Gymnasium is deeply rooted in values such as learning and creativity, diversity and tolerance, fairness and trust. These principles are symbolized by the school's "Michaeli-Drache" and significantly shape the positive school climate and strong community.

Among the outstanding additional offerings are the choir class (Chorklasse) and the wind instrument class (Bläserklasse), which nurture musical talents, as well as a dynamic theater group that promotes creative expression. Another important commitment of the school is migration support (Migrationsförderung), which aims to comprehensively integrate and support students with a migration background.

The architecture of the school building, characteristic of the early 1970s, presents itself in a sober concrete construction that prioritizes functionality. Its central location in Berg am Laim not only offers good accessibility but also the advantages of an urban environment with diverse recreational opportunities. For comprehensive student care, an all-day program (Ganztagsangebot) and a canteen for lunch (Mittagsverpflegung) are available. The school is led by Headmaster Frank Jung, who significantly shapes the institution's pedagogical vision.
summary_en: Founded in 1971, Michaeli-Gymnasium Munich is a state-run Gymnasium in Berg am Laim, focusing on linguistic and scientific-technological profiles. It offers 1268 students a broad curriculum including MINT, four languages, and artistic and social programs like choir, wind instrument, and theater classes, plus migration support. Values such as diversity and trust shape school life under the leadership of Frank Jung.
summary_de: Das 1971 gegründete Michaeli-Gymnasium München ist ein staatliches Gymnasium in Berg am Laim mit sprachlichem und naturwissenschaftlich-technologischem Schwerpunkt. description:
Gymnasium München-Nord, founded in 2016, is a state-run public school located in the Milbertshofen-Am Hart district of Munich. It combines the profiles of a linguistic and a scientific-technological Gymnasium and is also recognized as an Elite School of Sports and an Elite School of Football. With approximately 1036 students and 84 teachers, the school offers a comprehensive educational program. A key feature is its pedagogical framework, which is based on a child and youth-friendly rhythmization of the school day, aiming to enable deeper and more sustainable learning through a time-decoupled lesson organization – the 'more time' concept. Lessons are primarily conducted in double periods, supplemented by modular or epochal teaching from the 7th grade and interdisciplinary projects to foster networked thinking. 

The school operates on a 'Lernhauskonzept' (learning house concept), which divides the school into manageable units where classrooms are grouped around multifunctional central areas for teamwork and independent study. The 'Campus-Plus-Konzept' aims to decelerate the school day, partly through supervised study periods in the lower grades, supported by core subject teachers and the cooperation partner 'Essakoff teach and care'. description:
Gymnasium Kirchheim b. München is a state-run educational institution founded in 1982, located in the municipality of Kirchheim near Munich, in the eastern district of Munich. With approximately 1498 students and 108 teachers (as of the 2024/25 school year), it is one of the larger high schools in the region. The school offers both a scientific-technological and a linguistic branch, with English, Latin, and French as languages. 

The pedagogical concept of Gymnasium Kirchheim is characterized by a strong focus on MINT (Mathematics, Informatics, Natural Sciences, Technology) education. It is a MINT-EC school, a TUM-Reference School, and has been recognized as a MINT-friendly school. Furthermore, it was a model school in the HoriZONTec pilot project. A special offering is the bilingual program, where students from the 7th grade onwards are taught history in English, with the option to continue in the upper secondary level. For the lower grades, there are string classes. The subject 'Zeit für uns' (Time for Us) in grades 7 to 10 underscores the commitment to students' personal development. The school is also a prize-winning school of the i.s.i. Innovation Award and the German School Award 2017, and holds distinctions such as 'Environmental School in Europe' and 'School without Racism - School with Courage'. 

The facilities include a school building occupied in 1984 and expanded multiple times, featuring a three-part sports hall. A new school building on the opposite site was decided upon in 2015, and the groundbreaking has taken place, indicating a future modern infrastructure, although the project has faced criticism regarding delays and costs. 

In terms of childcare and support, Gymnasium Kirchheim offers an open all-day school program as well as a structured all-day class for grades 5 and 6, where students are supervised from Monday to Thursday until 4:00 PM. Additionally, there is an optional, voluntary afternoon program.
summary_en: Gymnasium Kirchheim b. München is a state-run high school founded in 1982, offering scientific-technological and linguistic branches. The school provides open and structured all-day care and has received numerous awards, including the German School Award 2017.
